value.title: Multiletter UV scalar converse tensorization

scopeQualifications: Exact additivity of B_avg applies to arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBC products; equality and additivity for B_br are established only under receiver-exchanging involutive input symmetry and its finite-product closure.

The functionals use separately optimized concave-envelope relaxations of the two UV sum-rate rows. The result does not establish tensorization of the complete UV region, simultaneous attainment by a common joint (U,V), other weighted scalarizations, the simplified GK functional, or the full Theorem-9 system.

The BSSC specialization depends on the previously established sharp one-letter BSSC posterior-support inequality and its equality-achieving posterior mixture; the general product-additivity and symmetry arguments are established internally.
The resulting BSSC converse value is non-frontier because it exceeds an already governed stronger benchmark; it proves neither achievability nor a capacity formula.

The contextual assertion that 0.369296945969202842443 is a certified full-Theorem-9 bound lacks terminal attestation in this packet, is not used as a premise, and does not affect the accepted theorem.
No objective execution attestations were supplied. The scripts and hash statements are corroborative only; the theorem is supported by the analytic proof.
value.statement: For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel W, let t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z), let 𝔠 be the upper concave envelope on the input simplex, and define A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+𝔠[-t_W](p), D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+𝔠[t_W](p), B_avg(W)=sup_p (A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2, and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. For arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBCs W_1 and W_2, B_avg(W_1×W_2)=B_avg(W_1)+B_avg(W_2), even when the product-channel input law is correlated and the envelope auxiliary is joint across factors. If an involutive input relabeling exchanges a channel's receivers, then B_br(W)=B_avg(W), and the optimization may be restricted to invariant input laws. Finite products preserve this receiver-skew symmetry, so for every finite family of such channels both scalar functionals are exactly additive. For the half-skew BSSC P, whose unique invariant binary prior is fair, combining these conclusions with the established sharp BSSC posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving posterior mixture gives B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) for every finite n≥1, with normalized value 0.3725562489182657... bits per channel use. This BSSC value is a valid but non-frontier UV converse and does not change the governed capacity interval.

computations: Corroborative audits check randomized and hostile product-channel chain identities, mutual-information subadditivity, product posterior mixtures, the BSSC symmetry maps, and the 90-digit evaluation of 2h_2(1/4)-5/4.
methods: Symmetrization of input laws under the receiver-exchanging involution and finite-product closure of that symmetry.
Upper-concave-envelope factorization with forward/reverse chain rules, including cancellation of the cross-coordinate co-information term at equal weighting.
proofs: Envelope covariance under a receiver-exchanging involution and concavity at the symmetrized input law prove B_br=B_avg and restriction to invariant laws; coordinatewise relabeling extends the conclusion to finite products.

Exact chain-rule cancellation for correlated product-channel inputs, followed by one-factor envelope bounds and concavity, proves the product upper bound; product priors and product posterior decompositions prove the reverse inequality for B_avg.

The half-skew BSSC specialization combines the symmetry and product theorem with the established sharp posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving mixture to obtain the exact symbolic value for every finite blocklength.
tools: Python 3 script verify_uv_hostile_cases.py checks deterministic and zero-probability cases and high-precision BSSC evaluation; neither script is an objective execution attestation.
Python 3 standard-library script verify_uv_factorization.py provides randomized numerical corroboration of the factorization identities.

topologyRationale: The new leaf is activated by the question whether multiletter coupling can strengthen UV-derived scalar converses and can be continued, stopped, or pruned independently of support reduction and channel-specific refinement for code-induced laws. Root is the narrowest existing parent because no existing program has a UV-functional tensorization objective. No additional grouping parent or child split is introduced: universal B_avg factorization, symmetry-based B_br equality, finite-product closure, and the BSSC corollary form one dependency-ordered theorem chain and jointly settle the same continue-or-stop decision for these separately relaxed scalar rows.
